newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN SEEKS CLASSIC GIANT SLALOM RESULT.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN SEEKS CLASSIC GIANT SLALOM RESULT.

text.p: Michael von Gruenigen skis the same way he lives his life - quietly and smoothly.
It is a style that keeps the 27-year-old Swiss content away from the World Cup slopes and successful on them.

Without the fanfare of his flamboyant rival Alberto Tomba, von Gruenigen has quietly established himself as one of circuit's all-time great technical skiers and can take his place in the World Cup record book, alongside the Italian, with a victory in Tuesday's giant slalom.

A win in his home canton will not only give von Gruenigen his third giant slalom victory of the season but a sweep of the discipline's three classics, Alta Badia, Kranjska Gora and Adelboden, in the same season. A feat accomplished only once before -- by Tomba.

Even the great Ingemar Stenmark, with 46 giant slalom wins, Marc Girardelli, the five-times overall World Cup champion and fabled Swiss all-rounder Pirmin Zurbriggen failed in their attempts to claim giant slalom's grand slam.
"This year my goal is to do well in the classics and to win in front of my fans at home would be special," said von Gruenigen, who shuns the spotlight the same way Tomba seeks it out.
While von Gruenigen may be joining Tomba in the record books, the Italian will not join him in the start hut on Tuesday.

Tomba, now battling 'flu and with a still tender wrist, was forced to pull out of Sunday's slalom in Chamonix after the first run and will not race in Adelboden, the final giant slalom tune-up before next month's world championships. That means he will have to defend his giant slalom title in Sestriere without completing a giant slalom race this season.

In Tomba's absence, von Gruenigen's biggest challenge is likely to come from Austria's Hans Knaus, who has yet to win a giant this season but has been placed among the top five in four out of five races.
Two of von Gruenigen's team mates, Steve Locher, winner of the season's first giant slalom and Urs Kaelin, the Olympic and world championship silver medallist, could also pose threats.
If von Gruenigen is to be denied a second consecutive victory on Adelboden's demanding Kuonisbergli course, it will require a special effort.

After a dominating performance at the last giant slalom in Kranjska Gora, where his margin of victory was almost two seconds, von Gruenigen underlined his superb form on Sunday with a fourth in the slalom.
In the 14 giant slaloms since the start of last season, von Gruenigen has won seven and failed to reach the podium only twice.
The shy Swiss will also enter the race as leader of both the overall World Cup and giant slalom standings.
A win would all but lock up a second straight giant slalom title for von Gruenigen but his stay on top of the overall rankings is likely to be brief.

While the overall crown usually goes to the skier who excels in all four Alpine disciplines, a quirk in the schedule has two specialists leading the rankings, von Gruenigen holding a slim 15-point advantage over slalom supremo Thomas Sykora of Austria.
Von Gruenigen depends almost solely on the giant slalom for his points and with six-of-eight giants gone after Tuesday's race, will have played most of his trump cards.
If von Gruenigen hopes to wear the coveted overall crown he will have to gleen more points from the slalom.
Although he has never won a World Cup slalom and finished in the top five only three times, there are signs he is beginning to translate some of his giant slalom success into the slalom.

"I am at my best level ever in giant right now which is why I will devote more of my training right now to the slalom," von Gruenigen, bronze medallist in both the slalom and giant slalom at last year's world championships, said. "But the overall title is not a goal for me at the moment because other skiers compete in so many more events.
"My goal is to defend my giant slalom title and win medals at the world championships."
